title: पञ्चषष्टितमोऽध्यायः
titleEn: Adhyaya 65 · The duel of Karna and Arjuna begins

summary.en: Karna and Arjuna meet with great din of conches and drums, and the arrows of each cut the other's. Krishna tells Arjuna to strike, and the fight grows fierce as the gods and creatures look on.
summary.kn: ಶಂಖ, ಭೇರಿಗಳ ಘೋಷದೊಂದಿಗೆ ಕರ್ಣ-ಅರ್ಜುನರು ಸಂಧಿಸುತ್ತಾರೆ; ಒಬ್ಬರ ಬಾಣಗಳು ಇನ್ನೊಬ್ಬರದನ್ನು ಕತ್ತರಿಸುತ್ತವೆ. ಹೊಡೆಯಲು ಕೃಷ್ಣ ಅರ್ಜುನನಿಗೆ ಹೇಳುತ್ತಾನೆ; ದೇವತೆಗಳು, ಜೀವಿಗಳು ನೋಡುತ್ತಿರಲು ಯುದ್ಧ ಉಗ್ರವಾಗುತ್ತದೆ.
summary.hi: शंखों और नगाड़ों के घोष के साथ कर्ण और अर्जुन मिलते हैं, और दोनों के बाण एक-दूसरे को काटते हैं। कृष्ण अर्जुन से प्रहार करने को कहते हैं, और देवताओं तथा प्राणियों के देखते युद्ध उग्र हो जाता है।
summary.te: శంఖ, భేరీ ధ్వనులతో కర్ణార్జునులు కలుస్తారు; ఒకరి బాణాలను మరొకరు ఛేదిస్తారు. కొట్టమని కృష్ణుడు అర్జునునికి చెబుతాడు; దేవతలు, జీవులు చూస్తుండగా పోరు భీకరమవుతుంది.
summary.ta: சங்கும் முரசும் முழங்க கர்ணனும் அர்ஜுனனும் சந்திக்கின்றனர்; ஒருவரின் அம்புகளை மற்றவர் வெட்டுகின்றனர். தாக்கும்படி கண்ணன் அர்ஜுனனிடம் கூற, தேவரும் உயிர்களும் பார்க்க போர் கடுமையாகிறது.
summary.ml: ശംഖുകളുടെയും ചെണ്ടകളുടെയും മഹാനാദത്തോടെ കർണ്ണനും അർജുനനും ഏറ്റുമുട്ടുന്നു; ഓരോരുത്തരുടെയും അമ്പുകൾ മറ്റവന്റെ അമ്പുകളെ മുറിക്കുന്നു. കൃഷ്ണൻ അർജുനനോട് പ്രഹരിക്കാൻ പറയുന്നു; ദേവന്മാരും ജീവികളും നോക്കിനിൽക്കെ പോരാട്ടം കടുക്കുന്നു.

source: Mahabharata, Critical Edition (BORI, Pune) 8.65; e-text by M. Tokunaga and J. D. Smith, © BORI 1999, version of Mon Jul 29 2019

verses.text: संजय उवाच

meaning.en: Sanjaya said:

verses.text:
तौ शङ्खभेरीनिनदे समृद्धे
समीयतुः श्वेतहयौ नराग्र्यौ ।
वैकर्तनः सूतपुत्रोऽर्जुनश्च
दुर्मन्त्रिते तव पुत्रस्य राजन् ॥

meaning.en: As conches and kettledrums sounded loudly, those two best of men with white horses, Karna Vaikartana the charioteer's son and Arjuna, came together, O king, because of your son's evil counsel.

verses.text:
यथा गजौ हैमवतौ प्रभिन्नौ
प्रगृह्य दन्ताविव वाशितार्थे ।
तथा समाजग्मतुरुग्रवेगौ
धनंजयश्चाधिरथिश्च वीरौ ॥

meaning.en: As two rutting elephants of the Himalaya clash with their tusks for the sake of a cow elephant, so the two heroes Dhananjaya and the son of Adhiratha met in fierce rush.

verses.text:
बलाहकेनेव यथा बलाहको
यदृच्छया वा गिरिणा गिरिर्यथा ।
तथा धनुर्ज्यातलनेमिनिस्वनौ
समीयतुस्ताविषुवर्षवर्षिणौ ॥

meaning.en: They met like cloud against cloud or mountain against mountain by chance, with the sound of bows, strings, palms and wheel-rims, each showering rains of arrows.

verses.text:
प्रवृद्धशृङ्गद्रुमवीरुदोषधी
प्रवृद्धनानाविधपर्वतौकसौ ।
यथाचलौ वा गलितौ महाबलौ
तथा महास्त्रैरितरेतरं घ्नतः ॥

meaning.en: Like two great mountains with high peaks, trees, creepers, herbs and many sorts of creatures dwelling on them, mighty and shaken loose, they struck each other with great missiles.

verses.text:
स संनिपातस्तु तयोर्महानभू-
त्सुरेशवैरोचनयोर्यथा पुरा ।
शरैर्विभुग्नाङ्गनियन्तृवाहनः
सुदुःसहोऽन्यैः पटुशोणितोदकः ॥

meaning.en: That clash of the two was as great as that of the lord of the gods and Virochana's son long ago: with limbs, drivers and mounts broken by arrows, and rivers of blood flowing, hard for others to bear.

verses.text:
प्रभूतपद्मोत्पलमत्स्यकच्छपौ
महाह्रदौ पक्षिगणानुनादितौ ।
सुसंनिकृष्टावनिलोद्धतौ यथा
तथा रथौ तौ ध्वजिनौ समीयतुः ॥

meaning.en: The two chariots with banners met like two great lakes full of lotuses, blue lilies, fish and tortoises, resounded with flocks of birds, close together and stirred by wind.

verses.text:
उभौ महेन्द्रस्य समानविक्रमा-
वुभौ महेन्द्रप्रतिमौ महारथौ ।
महेन्द्रवज्रप्रतिमैश्च सायकै-
र्महेन्द्रवृत्राविव संप्रजह्रतुः ॥

meaning.en: Both were equal in valor to great Indra, both were great chariot-warriors like Mahendra, and with arrows like Indra's thunderbolt they struck each other as Mahendra and Vritra did.

verses.text:
सनागपत्त्यश्वरथे उभे बले
विचित्रवर्णाभरणाम्बरस्रजे ।
चकम्पतुश्चोन्नमतः स्म विस्मया-
द्वियद्गताश्चार्जुनकर्णसंयुगे ॥

meaning.en: The two armies, with elephants, foot soldiers, horses and chariots, in varied colors, ornaments, garments and garlands, shook and rose up with wonder, as those in the sky watched the fight of Arjuna and Karna.

verses.text:
भुजाः सवज्राङ्गुलयः समुच्छ्रिताः
ससिंहनादा हृषितैर्दिदृक्षुभिः ।
यदार्जुनं मत्तमिव द्विपो द्विपं
समभ्ययादाधिरथिर्जिघांसया ॥

meaning.en: Arms with fingers like thunderbolts were raised, with lion-roars from delighted onlookers, as the son of Adhiratha, wishing to kill, rushed at Arjuna like one elephant at another in rut.

verses.text:
अभ्यक्रोशन्सोमकास्तत्र पार्थं
त्वरस्व याह्यर्जुन विध्य कर्णम् ।
छिन्ध्यस्य मूर्धानमलं चिरेण
श्रद्धां च राज्याद्धृतराष्ट्रसूनोः ॥

meaning.en: The Somakas cried out there to Partha, "Hurry, go, Arjuna, pierce Karna! Cut off his head, and the hope of Dhritarashtra's son for the kingdom, without delay!"

verses.text:
तथास्माकं बहवस्तत्र योधाः
कर्णं तदा याहि याहीत्यवोचन् ।
जह्यर्जुनं कर्ण ततः सचीराः
पुनर्वनं यान्तु चिराय पार्थाः ॥

meaning.en: And many warriors on our side said to Karna, "Go, go, kill Arjuna, Karna, and let the Parthas go to the forest again in bark garments for a long time."

verses.text:
ततः कर्णः प्रथमं तत्र पार्थं
महेषुभिर्दशभिः पर्यविध्यत् ।
तमर्जुनः प्रत्यविध्यच्छिताग्रैः
कक्षान्तरे दशभिरतीव क्रुद्धः ॥

meaning.en: Then Karna first pierced Partha there with ten great arrows, and Arjuna, in great rage, pierced him in return with ten sharp-tipped ones in the armpit.

verses.text:
परस्परं तौ विशिखैः सुतीक्ष्णै-
स्ततक्षतुः सूतपुत्रोऽर्जुनश्च ।
परस्परस्यान्तरेप्सू विमर्दे
सुभीममभ्याययतुः प्रहृष्टौ ॥

meaning.en: The charioteer's son and Arjuna cut each other with very sharp arrows; each seeking an opening in the other in the clash, they came on delighted into the terrible fight.

verses.text:
अमृष्यमाणश्च महाविमर्दे
तत्राक्रुध्यद्भीमसेनो महात्मा ।
अथाब्रवीत्पाणिना पाणिमाघ्न-
न्संदष्टौष्ठो नृत्यति वादयन्निव ।
कथं नु त्वां सूतपुत्रः किरीटि-
न्महेषुभिर्दशभिरविध्यदग्रे ॥

meaning.en: Unable to bear the great struggle, the great-souled Bhimasena there grew angry. He struck palm on palm, biting his lip, as if dancing and drumming, and said: "How was it that the charioteer's son pierced you first with ten great arrows, diadem-wearer?

verses.text:
यया धृत्या सर्वभूतान्यजैषी-
र्ग्रासं ददद्वह्नये खाण्डवे त्वम् ।
तया धृत्या सूतपुत्रं जहि त्व-
महं वैनं गदया पोथयिष्ये ॥

meaning.en: With the firmness with which you conquered all beings and gave Agni his meal in Khandava, with that firmness kill the charioteer's son; or else I will crush him with my mace."

verses.text:
अथाब्रवीद्वासुदेवोऽपि पार्थं
दृष्ट्वा रथेषून्प्रतिहन्यमानान् ।
अमीमृदत्सर्वथा तेऽद्य कर्णो
ह्यस्त्रैरस्त्राणि किमिदं किरीटिन् ॥

meaning.en: Then Vasudeva too spoke to Partha, seeing his arrows struck back in the chariots: "Karna has crushed your missiles completely today with his own missiles; what is this, diadem-wearer?

verses.text:
स वीर किं मुह्यसि नावधीयसे
नदन्त्येते कुरवः संप्रहृष्टाः ।
कर्णं पुरस्कृत्य विदुर्हि सर्वे
त्वदस्त्रमस्त्रैर्विनिपात्यमानम् ॥

meaning.en: Hero, why are you confused and not attentive? These Kurus roar, delighted; they all know that Karna, put forward, is bringing down your weapon with weapons.

verses.text:
यया धृत्या निहतं तामसास्त्रं
युगे युगे राक्षसाश्चापि घोराः ।
दम्भोद्भवाश्चासुराश्चाहवेषु
तया धृत्या त्वं जहि सूतपुत्रम् ॥

meaning.en: With the steadiness with which you destroyed the Tamasa missile, and in age after age the fearsome Rakshasas and the Asuras born of pride in battles, with that firmness kill the charioteer's son.

verses.text:
अनेन वास्य क्षुरनेमिनाद्य
संछिन्द्धि मूर्धानमरेः प्रसह्य ।
मया निसृष्टेन सुदर्शनेन
वज्रेण शक्रो नमुचेरिवारेः ॥

meaning.en: Today forcibly cut off this enemy's head with this razor-rimmed Sudarshana, sent by me, as Indra did with his thunderbolt to Namuchi, his foe.

verses.text:
किरातरूपी भगवान्यया च
त्वया महत्या परितोषितोऽभूत् ।
तां त्वं धृतिं वीर पुनर्गृहीत्वा
सहानुबन्धं जहि सूतपुत्रम् ॥

meaning.en: With the great firmness by which you pleased the lord who came in the form of a Kirata, take up that firmness again, hero, and kill the charioteer's son with his followers.

verses.text:
ततो महीं सागरमेखलां त्वं
सपत्तनां ग्रामवतीं समृद्धाम् ।
प्रयच्छ राज्ञे निहतारिसंघां
यशश्च पार्थातुलमाप्नुहि त्वम् ॥

meaning.en: Then give to the king the earth, with its girdle of oceans, its towns and villages and its prosperity, with the hosts of his enemies slain, and win, Partha, matchless fame."

verses.text:
संचोदितो भीमजनार्दनाभ्यां
स्मृत्वा तदात्मानमवेक्ष्य सत्त्वम् ।
महात्मनश्चागमने विदित्वा
प्रयोजनं केशवमित्युवाच ॥

meaning.en: Urged on by Bhima and Janardana, Arjuna remembered himself, considered his strength, understood the purpose of the great one's coming, and said to Keshava:

verses.text:
प्रादुष्करोम्येष महास्त्रमुग्रं
शिवाय लोकस्य वधाय सौतेः ।
तन्मेऽनुजानातु भवान्सुराश्च
ब्रह्मा भवो ब्रह्मविदश्च सर्वे ॥

meaning.en: "I now bring out a fierce great missile for the good of the world and for the death of the charioteer's son. Let you, the gods, Brahma, Bhava and all knowers of Brahman allow me."

verses.text:
इत्यूचिवान्ब्राह्ममसह्यमस्त्रं
प्रादुश्चक्रे मनसा संविधेयम् ।
ततो दिशश्च प्रदिशश्च सर्वाः
समावृणोत्सायकैर्भूरितेजाः ।
ससर्ज बाणान्भरतर्षभोऽपि
शतंशतानेकवदाशुवेगान् ॥

meaning.en: Having said this, he brought forth the unbearable Brahma missile, which is controlled by the mind. Then the very radiant one covered all directions and intermediate directions with arrows, and the best of the Bharatas loosed hundreds of arrows, swift, all as if one.

verses.text:
वैकर्तनेनापि तथाजिमध्ये
सहस्रशो बाणगणा विसृष्टाः ।
ते घोषिणः पाण्डवमभ्युपेयुः
पर्जन्यमुक्ता इव वारिधाराः ॥

meaning.en: Karna too, in the midst of the battle, loosed thousands of showers of arrows; they came roaring at the Pandava like streams of rain loosed by a cloud.

verses.text:
स भीमसेनं च जनार्दनं च
किरीटिनं चाप्यमनुष्यकर्मा ।
त्रिभिस्त्रिभिर्भीमबलो निहत्य
ननाद घोरं महता स्वरेण ॥

meaning.en: With three arrows each he struck Bhimasena, Janardana and the diadem-wearer, that man of superhuman deeds and fearful strength, and roared a dreadful roar with a great voice.

verses.text:
स कर्णबाणाभिहतः किरीटी
भीमं तथा प्रेक्ष्य जनार्दनं च ।
अमृष्यमाणः पुनरेव पार्थः
शरान्दशाष्टौ च समुद्बबर्ह ॥

meaning.en: Struck by Karna's arrows, and seeing Bhima and Janardana struck too, the diadem-wearer Partha, unable to bear it, drew out eighteen arrows again.

verses.text:
सुषेणमेकेन शरेण विद्ध्वा
शल्यं चतुर्भिस्त्रिभिरेव कर्णम् ।
ततः सुमुक्तैर्दशभिर्जघान
सभापतिं काञ्चनवर्मनद्धम् ॥

meaning.en: With one arrow he pierced Sushena, with four Shalya and with three Karna; then with ten well-loosed arrows he killed the Sabhapati, who was clad in golden armor.

verses.text:
स राजपुत्रो विशिरा विबाहु-
र्विवाजिसूतो विधनुर्विकेतुः ।
ततो रथाग्रादपतत्प्रभग्नः
परश्वधैः शाल इवाभिकृत्तः ॥

meaning.en: That prince, without head, arms, horses, charioteer, bow or banner, fell shattered from the front of his chariot, like a sal tree cut down by axes.

verses.text:
पुनश्च कर्णं त्रिभिरष्टभिश्च
द्वाभ्यां चतुर्भिर्दशभिश्च विद्ध्वा ।
चतुःशतान्द्विरदान्सायुधीया-
न्हत्वा रथानष्टशतं जघान ।
सहस्रमश्वांश्च पुनश्च सादी-
नष्टौ सहस्राणि च पत्तिवीरान् ॥

meaning.en: Then, piercing Karna again with three, eight, two, four and ten arrows, he killed four hundred armed elephants, eight hundred chariots, a thousand horses and horsemen, and eight thousand foot soldiers.

verses.text:
दृष्ट्वाजिमुख्यावथ युध्यमानौ
दिदृक्षवः शूरवरावरिघ्नौ ।
कर्णं च पार्थं च नियम्य वाहा-
न्खस्था महीस्थाश्च जनावतस्थुः ॥

meaning.en: Seeing those two chiefs of the battle fighting, those eager to watch the best of heroes, slayers of foes, halted their mounts, both those in the sky and those on earth, and stood to watch Karna and Partha.

verses.text:
ततो धनुर्ज्या सहसातिकृष्टा
सुघोषमाच्छिद्यत पाण्डवस्य ।
तस्मिन्क्षणे सूतपुत्रस्तु पार्थं
समाचिनोत्क्षुद्रकाणां शतेन ॥

meaning.en: Then the Pandava's bowstring, which made a fine sound, was suddenly drawn too hard and snapped; at that moment the charioteer's son covered Partha with a hundred small arrows.

verses.text:
निर्मुक्तसर्पप्रतिमैश्च तीक्ष्णै-
स्तैलप्रधौतैः खगपत्रवाजैः ।
षष्ट्या नाराचैर्वासुदेवं बिभेद
तदन्तरं सोमकाः प्राद्रवन्त ॥

meaning.en: With sixty sharp iron arrows like shed snakes, washed in oil, fletched with bird feathers, he pierced Vasudeva; and in that interval the Somakas rushed forward.

verses.text:
ततो धनुर्ज्यामवधम्य शीघ्रं
शरानस्तानाधिरथेर्विधम्य ।
सुसंरब्धः कर्णशरक्षताङ्गो
रणे पार्थः सोमकान्प्रत्यगृह्णात् ।
न पक्षिणः संपतन्त्यन्तरिक्षे
क्षेपीयसास्त्रेण कृतेऽन्धकारे ॥

meaning.en: Then Arjuna quickly strung his bow and scattered the arrows loosed by the son of Adhiratha; furious, his limbs wounded by Karna's arrows, he protected the Somakas in the battle. Not even birds could fly in the sky, which was made dark by his swift missile.

verses.text:
शल्यं च पार्थो दशभिः पृषत्कै-
र्भृशं तनुत्रे प्रहसन्नविध्यत् ।
ततः कर्णं द्वादशभिः सुमुक्तै-
र्विद्ध्वा पुनः सप्तभिरभ्यविध्यत् ॥

meaning.en: Partha, smiling, pierced Shalya hard in the armor with ten arrows, then pierced Karna with twelve well-loosed ones, and again with seven.

verses.text:
स पार्थबाणासनवेगनुन्नै-
र्दृढाहतः पत्रिभिरुग्रवेगैः ।
विभिन्नगात्रः क्षतजोक्षिताङ्गः
कर्णो बभौ रुद्र इवाततेषुः ॥

meaning.en: Driven by Partha's bow with force, hard struck by fierce, swift arrows, his body split and his limbs drenched in blood, Karna shone like Rudra with bow drawn.

verses.text:
ततस्त्रिभिश्च त्रिदशाधिपोपमं
शरैर्बिभेदाधिरथिर्धनंजयम् ।
शरांस्तु पञ्च ज्वलितानिवोरगा-
न्प्रवीरयामास जिघांसुरच्युते ॥

meaning.en: Then the son of Adhiratha pierced Dhananjaya, who was like the lord of the gods, with three arrows, and sent five arrows like blazing serpents at Achyuta, wishing to kill him.

verses.text:
ते वर्म भित्त्वा पुरुषोत्तमस्य
सुवर्णचित्रं न्यपतन्सुमुक्ताः ।
वेगेन गामाविविशुः सुवेगाः
स्नात्वा च कर्णाभिमुखाः प्रतीयुः ॥

meaning.en: They pierced the armor of that best of men and, well loosed, fell splendid with gold; swift, they entered the earth with force, and having bathed there, returned toward Karna.

verses.text:
तान्पञ्चभल्लैस्त्वरितैः सुमुक्तै-
स्त्रिधा त्रिधैकैकमथोच्चकर्त ।
धनंजयस्ते न्यपतन्पृथिव्यां
महाहयस्तक्षकपुत्रपक्षाः ॥

meaning.en: Dhananjaya swiftly cut each of them in three with five well-loosed broad-headed arrows; they fell to earth like great serpents, partisans of Takshaka's son.

verses.text:
ततः प्रजज्वाल किरीटमाली
क्रोधेन कक्षं प्रदहन्निवाग्निः ।
स कर्णमाकर्णविकृष्टसृष्टैः
शरैः शरीरान्तकरैर्ज्वलद्भिः ।
मर्मस्वविध्यत्स चचाल दुःखा-
द्धैर्यात्तु तस्थावतिमात्रधैर्यः ॥

meaning.en: Then the diadem-wearer blazed with anger, burning like fire on a thicket; with arrows drawn to the ear and loosed, blazing and ending bodies, he pierced Karna in his vital spots; Karna wavered in pain, but stood firm with great firmness.

verses.text:
ततः शरौघैः प्रदिशो दिशश्च
रविप्रभा कर्णरथश्च राजन् ।
अदृश्य आसीत्कुपिते धनंजये
तुषारनीहारवृतं यथा नभः ॥

meaning.en: Then, O king, with floods of arrows the directions and intermediate directions, the sun's light and Karna's chariot were hidden when Dhananjaya was enraged, as the sky is hidden by frost and mist.

verses.text:
स चक्ररक्षानथ पादरक्षा-
न्पुरःसरान्पृष्ठगोपांश्च सर्वान् ।
दुर्योधनेनानुमतानरिघ्ना-
न्समुच्चितान्सुरथान्सारभूतान् ॥

meaning.en: Arjuna, the left-handed archer, then destroyed the wheel-guards, the foot-guards, the front fighters and the rear guards, all chosen, excellent chariot-warriors approved by Duryodhana, slayers of foes.

verses.text:
द्विसाहस्रान्समरे सव्यसाची
कुरुप्रवीरानृषभः कुरूणाम् ।
क्षणेन सर्वान्सरथाश्वसूता-
न्निनाय राजन्क्षयमेकवीरः ॥

meaning.en: That bull of the Kurus, the lone hero Savyasachi, sent all two thousand Kuru heroes in the battle, with their chariots, horses and charioteers, to destruction in an instant, O king.

verses.text:
अथापलायन्त विहाय कर्णं
तवात्मजाः कुरवश्चावशिष्टाः ।
हतानवाकीर्य शरक्षतांश्च
लालप्यमानांस्तनयान्पितॄंश्च ॥

meaning.en: Then your sons and the remaining Kurus fled, abandoning Karna and leaving behind the slain and the arrow-wounded, who were lamenting for their sons and fathers.

verses.text:
स सर्वतः प्रेक्ष्य दिशो विशून्या
भयावदीर्णैः कुरुभिर्विहीनः ।
न विव्यथे भारत तत्र कर्णः
प्रतीपमेवार्जुनमभ्यधावत् ॥

meaning.en: Seeing all quarters emptied and himself left without Kurus, who were torn apart by fear, Karna was not shaken there, O Bharata, but ran straight at Arjuna.
